rows.text:
Ines Okafor is the new keeper of the Salt Ledger on Harrow Quay. Tobiah Wren is the ferryman who delivered Ines Okafor to the island. Ines Okafor must finish the audit before the equinox market.

Tobiah Wren informs Ines Okafor that the previous keeper, Aldous Brandt, did not simply leave. Mara Venn reveals that the spring pages of the Salt Ledger are missing. Ines Okafor went to the net loft to find anyone who had worked with Aldous Brandt. Mara Lisle revealed that Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping and went to the salt warehouse at night with a lantern. Mara Lisle stated that Aldous Brandt came back from the warehouse with chalk on his sleeves while counting barrels. Ines Okafor counted the salt and discovered twenty-four barrels a month had come onto the island and never reached the book. On the fourth evening she found a printed handbill pasted over the margin of the November page.

Ines dropped the handbill in the stove and went on working. Ines Okafor took the handbill for a prank by the dock boys who pasted rude verses on everything. Did Mara Lisle steal the ledger pages as the handbill instructed Ines Okafor to state?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor is the new keeper of the Salt Ledger on Harrow Quay. Aldous Brandt was the previous keeper who disappeared three weeks ago. Ines Okafor must finish the audit before the equinox market.

Tobiah Wren warned Ines Okafor that the previous keeper did not simply leave. Ines Okafor counted the salt and found twenty-four barrels missing from the ledger. Someone entered the archive at the foot of the tower and climbed the stairs. Ines Okafor copied her salt count onto a single sheet showing forty barrels in the book and sixty-four on the receipts. Ines Okafor worked late in the archive until a little before midnight.

Dr Pike found her on the tower steps and was all concern. He made her sit, and listened to the whole story with his hands folded. Who was the person who climbed the stairs and stole the tally sheet from Ines Okafor's desk?

Ines Okafor is the new keeper of the Salt Ledger on the island of Harrow Quay. Aldous Brandt was the previous keeper who disappeared three weeks ago. Mara Venn is the Harbourmaster who leads Ines Okafor to the archive. Dr Pike is the physician and printer who keeps the tide tables in his dispensary. Ines Okafor must finish the audit before the equinox market. The council must settle debts to refuse the Crane Company's offer.

Tobiah Wren warns Ines Okafor to trust the tide tables less than the water itself. Mara Venn reveals that the spring pages of the Salt Ledger are missing. Ines Okafor counted the salt and found twenty-four barrels missing from the ledger. Ines Okafor copied her salt count onto a single sheet showing forty barrels in the book and sixty-four on the receipts. Someone entered the archive at the foot of the tower and climbed the stairs. Ines Okafor worked late in the archive until a little before midnight. Dr Pike found Ines Okafor on the tower steps and was all concern. Dr Pike told Ines Okafor that she has met the Harbourmaster's coat. Dr Pike offered Ines Okafor a strongbox in the dispensary where nobody searches a doctor. Ines Okafor accepted Dr Pike's kind and sensible offer to store the receipts. Ines Okafor did not sleep at first light and searched the archive again. Ines Okafor searched the archive again at first light as if the tally might have fallen behind the desk.
